historical_timeline.summary: Born at Popes Creek farm, Westmoreland County, Virginia (February 11, Old Style).
Smallpox in Barbados at 19; recovers with slight scarring and lifelong immunity.
Dysentery with fever on the Braddock expedition; about five weeks to recover. Recurrent malarial fevers through his adult life.
At 24, pays to have a tooth removed; dental pain, decay and tooth loss from his twenties.
Wears false teeth wired to his remaining natural teeth.
His accounts record a payment to enslaved people at Mount Vernon for nine teeth, on the account of a visiting dentist.
Inaugurated as president in New York with one natural tooth left; full dentures of ivory and human teeth are made for him that year.
A large, painful tumor of the thigh is removed in New York; six weeks to heal.
Diary records an aching tooth with a swollen, inflamed gum.
Seized with a severe illness, described as pneumonia, after a cold; his life is despaired of before he recovers over several weeks.
Last natural tooth removed at 64; later complains that his dentures are uneasy and loose.
Dies at Mount Vernon at 67 of a throat infection, after repeated bloodletting; usually interpreted today as acute epiglottitis. At his death 317 enslaved people were held at Mount Vernon.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Tooth loss as a medical problem: a 57-year-old head of state in his first year in office, who has lost his teeth over thirty years, comes in because worn complete dentures hurt, move when he speaks in public and have narrowed his diet, with unintended weight loss. The episode covers an oral examination by the primary clinician with oral cancer screening and the two-week rule for an oral ulcer, nutrition screening with the MNA-SF and a focused weight-loss evaluation, the American College of Prosthodontists diagnostic index for complete edentulism, care and maintenance of complete dentures, new complete dentures and a mandibular two-implant overdenture as the first-choice standard under the McGill and York consensus statements, antibiotic prophylaxis at implant placement, speech and public speaking with new dentures, cardiovascular risk assessment with tooth loss recorded as an association only, and an outpatient community-acquired pneumonia managed with CURB-65 and the 2019 ATS/IDSA guideline in a man with healing implants.

visit_schedule.purpose: Establishing primary care for painful, loose dentures that make eating and speaking difficult, with weight loss: oral examination and oral cancer screening, nutrition screening, the evaluation of weight loss, and a prosthodontic referral

Twelve-week review: new complete dentures six weeks in use, three weeks after two lower implants were placed; eating, speech, weight and healing
Same-day sick visit for fever, cough and chest pain
Clinical resolution review two weeks after outpatient pneumonia, with the implant healing and weight
Six-month review: the implant-retained lower overdenture in use for three weeks; chewing, speech, nutrition and long-term maintenance

assessment.display: Complete edentulism, ACP diagnostic index class III
assessment.assessment: Complete edentulism of both jaws, class III by the American College of Prosthodontists diagnostic index because of the mandibular bone height of about 14 mm and the unfavorable lower ridge and muscle attachment. The worn dentures with a closed bite account for the pain, the instability and the change in the support of his lips. Relining the old dentures would not correct the worn teeth or the bite, so replacement is advised

The McGill and York consensus statements make a two-implant overdenture the first-choice standard for the edentulous lower jaw, with better chewing, comfort and satisfaction than a conventional denture. He is healthy, does not smoke, has no diabetes and takes no bone-modifying drug, and the panoramic radiograph suggests enough bone in the canine regions; a cone beam CT will confirm it. The upper denture is expected to do well without implants on his well-formed upper ridge

Poor chewing explains his narrowed diet and weight loss. New dentures need a few weeks of adaptation for chewing and speech; the lower denture will stay less stable than the upper until the attachments are connected

recommendations: Relieve the lower flange and reline the old lower denture with a tissue conditioner today, and keep it out overnight
New upper and lower complete dentures over the next four weeks, the lower designed for conversion to an implant overdenture, with an adjustment visit 24 hours to one week after delivery

Cone beam CT of the mandible, then two implants in the lower canine regions after the new dentures are delivered, with amoxicillin 2 g one hour before surgery, chlorhexidine rinses for two weeks and a short course of ibuprofen; the denture relieved and soft-lined over the implants; sutures out at about ten days
Connect stud attachments to the implants after about three months of healing, with a check within a week
Read aloud daily with the new dentures; a speech-language assessment if speech is not clear by six weeks
Continue the soft high-protein diet with the supplement until chewing is restored, and widen the diet as the new dentures settle
Clean the dentures daily with a soft brush and non-abrasive cleanser, keep them out overnight in water, and attend a yearly prosthodontic recall; replace the attachment inserts when retention falls
